result:
Nothing is built yet. The package is a greeting `main()` with two smoke tests, and no runtime dependencies. So this goes through the new-project entry. There's no spec: `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` is your research brief, and the three research files are background. Every outcome below is a **candidate** for you to confirm, cut or reword.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Source | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size by stage (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark), total nonfarm, from 1979 to now, shown over time with the 2003 and 2020–22 breaks marked | prompt Part A; chatgpt exec summary | Small to moderate. FRED API allows 120 requests/min. The BLS API serves only current vintages, so earlier prints come from ALFRED or archived releases. ALFRED's depth for PAYEMS is unconfirmed. |
| O2 | The same, by supersector, NSA and SA | prompt Part C (hierarchy, seasonality) | ALFRED supersector vintage coverage is unknown and may need archived releases. The core stage measures it. |
| O3 | SA one- and two-month revisions split into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part | prompt Part A §1; chatgpt calls this unstudied | Data cost depends on O2's NSA vintages. Method is open. |
| O4 | Whether collection days and first-closing rate move the scale of one-month revisions | prompt Part A §2 | Collection days come from calendar arithmetic and are cheap. Collection-rate history start is unconfirmed (Claude file cites a 2015 peak). |
| O5 | A descriptive account of revision scale against BLS appropriations, FTE and sample size, labelled non-causal | prompt Part A §3–5, Part C (identification) | Mostly your time: hand-built from roughly 40 annual budget justifications plus FedScope. Can't be estimated until one year is extracted. |
| O6 | The multi-vintage latent-state model: news and noise per stage, benchmark as an irregular observation with wedge-back, covariates in the log-scale with Student-t errors | prompt Part C | Compute unknown: about 550 months × 4 stages, ×2 with NSA/SA, ×11 supersectors if pooled. Only a timed fit can tell. |
| O7 | Validation of O6: revision-dispersion posterior predictive checks, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks | prompt Part C | Repeated fits multiply O6's cost. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision record (O1, O2). Known progression.** I'd expect total nonfarm first, then stage dispersion, then supersectors with NSA/SA. Tell me if you'd name the stages differently.
- **B: Seasonal vs. sample (O3). Research.** Split from C because either answer stands without the other.
- **C: Collection interval (O4). Research.** Split because it rests on within-year calendar variation and doesn't need the full model. Bundled into D, it would wait on that machinery.
- **D: Integrated model (O6, O7, and O5 as covariates). Research.** O5 could instead be its own descriptive track, so it doesn't wait on O6. I lean toward splitting it out, but it's your call.

All tracks consume Track A's vintage panel, so A's core stage will likely come first whatever the ranking.

## Choices already made
- Python 3.14 and uv, from the repo. JAX support on 3.14 is unverified and is worth checking early.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ and Polars, from the brief.

**Proposed name:** `ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

I based the cost notes on the brief and the research files' summaries. Before writing the roadmap, I'll read the data-availability inventories (chatgpt §3.3, gemini "Data Availability Inventory") to firm them up. I'd also like to run one probe: list ALFRED's PAYEMS vintage dates to confirm how far O1 reaches. I'll only run it if you say yes.

**One request:** rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (including whether O5 splits out), the name, and whether to run the probe.
